{% raw %}
`aplay`: play WAV files on a sound card.

## Synopsis

<strong>aplay</strong> \[<strong>-D</strong> <em>device</em>\] \[<em>file</em>...\]

## Description

<strong>aplay</strong> plays each WAV <em>file</em> on a sound card, one after another. With no <em>file</em>, or where a <em>file</em> is <strong>-</strong>, it reads standard input.

A file's header says its format, and <strong>aplay</strong> sets the card to it: PCM (unsigned 8-bit or signed 16-bit) or IMA ADPCM, mono or stereo, at 8000, 11025, 22050 or 44100 samples a second. It writes the file's data as it reads it (a write waits while the card's buffer is full), then waits for what it queued to play out before the next file.

A stereo sound comes from two speakers, the block's left and right as seen facing its front; a mono one from the block. Any other music can be converted on another computer, for example with <strong>ffmpeg</strong>:

```text
ffmpeg -i song.mp3 -ar 22050 -ac 2 -acodec adpcm_ima_wav song.wav
```

A file that cannot be opened, read or played is reported on standard error, and <strong>aplay</strong> goes on with the next one.

## Options

<strong>-D</strong> <em>device</em>
: The sound card's file (<strong>/dev/dsp</strong>, the first card's, unless given).

## Exit status

0 if every file was played; 1 if any could not be, or the card could not be opened.

## Examples

```text
aplay song.wav
aplay -D /dev/dsp1 alarm.wav
```

## Notes

ALSA's <strong>aplay</strong> has many more options (raw formats, recording with <strong>arecord</strong>, devices by name); mcos's takes WAV files only. A raw file plays as it is with <strong>cat file \> /dev/dsp</strong>, at OSS's defaults: 8000 samples a second, unsigned 8-bit, mono.

## See also

<strong>cat</strong>(1)
